'''Ginés Morata Pérez''' is a Spanish biologist who is Research [[Professor]] at the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]] in Spain<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=current>{{cite journal|last1=Morata|first1=Ginés|title=Ginés Morata|journal=[[Current Biology]]|volume=16|issue=23|year=2006|pages=R976–R977|issn=0960-9822|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2006.10.047|pmid= 17195314|doi-access=free|bibcode=2006CBio...16.R976M }}</ref> and an expert in [[developmental biology]] of the [[Drosophila|fruit fly (''Drosophila'')]], a specialty he has worked on for over 40 years.<ref name=formemrs/><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Morata|first1=Ginés|last2=Struhl|first2=Gary|s2cid=4464450|date=2014|title=Developmental biology: Tethered wings|journal=Nature|volume=505|issue=7482|pages=162–163|doi=10.1038/nature12848|issn=1476-4687|pmid=24390347|bibcode=2014Natur.505..162M|doi-access=free}} {{closed access}}</ref>

==Education==
Morata was educated at the {{ill|Universidad Laboral de Sevilla|es}} and the [[Complutense University of Madrid]]. He was awarded a PhD in 1973 for research on the [[heredity]] in the fruit fly ''[[Drosophila]]'' supervised by [[Antonio García-Bellido]].<ref name=morataphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Ginés|last=Morata Pérez |title=Herencia celular de la determinación en Drosophila |publisher=Universidad Complutense de Madrid |date=1973 |oclc=911990833 |id={{ProQuest|1832950364}}}}</ref>

==Career and research==
{{As of|2017}}, his research focuses on cell competition,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ballesteros-Arias|first1=L.|last2=Saavedra|first2=V.|last3=Morata|first3=G.|date=2014|title=Cell competition may function either as tumour-suppressing or as tumour-stimulating factor in Drosophila|journal=Oncogene|volume=33|issue=35|pages=4377–4384|doi=10.1038/onc.2013.407|issn=1476-5594|pmid=24096487|hdl=10261/118069|doi-access=free}} {{closed access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Morata|first1=Ginés|last2=Ballesteros-Arias|first2=Luna|date=2015|title=Cell competition, apoptosis and tumour development|journal=The International Journal of Developmental Biology|volume=59|issue=1–3|pages=79–86|doi=10.1387/ijdb.150081gm|issn=1696-3547|pmid=26374529|url=https://digital.csic.es/bitstream/10261/133288/1/Morata%20G%20Cell%20competition.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref> especially in relation to [[apoptosis]] and [[carcinogenesis]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Calleja|first1=Manuel|last2=Morata|first2=Ginés|last3=Casanova|first3=Jordi|date=2016|title=Tumorigenic Properties of Drosophila Epithelial Cells Mutant for lethal giant larvae|journal=[[Developmental Dynamics]]|volume=245|issue=8|pages=834–843|doi=10.1002/dvdy.24420|issn=1097-0177|pmid=27239786|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=eiger>{{Cite journal|last1=Morata|first1=Ginés|last2=Herrera|first2=Salvador C.|date=2013|title=Eiger triggers death from afar|journal=[[eLife]]|volume=2|article-number=e01388|doi=10.7554/eLife.01388|issn=2050-084X|pmc=3780540|pmid=24069529 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Herrera|first1=Salvador C.|last2=Martín|first2=Raquel|last3=Morata|first3=Ginés|date=2013|title=Tissue homeostasis in the wing disc of Drosophila melanogaster: immediate response to massive damage during development|journal=[[PLOS Genetics]]|volume=9|issue=4|article-number=e1003446|doi=10.1371/journal.pgen.1003446|issn=1553-7404|pmc=3636033|pmid=23633961 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref> His lab also does experimental analysis of regeneration in the [[imaginal disc]]s.

Morata  has been involved in several major discoveries, including the discovery of [[Compartment (development)|developmental compartments]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Herrera|first1=Salvador C.|last2=Morata|first2=Ginés|date=2014|title=Transgressions of compartment boundaries and cell reprogramming during regeneration in Drosophila|journal=eLife|volume=3|article-number=e01831|doi=10.7554/eLife.01831|issn=2050-084X|pmc=3989595|pmid=24755288 |doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref> the phenomenon of cell competition, the connection between genes and compartments, the elucidation of the structure of the [[Hox gene]] complex, and the discovery of [[mitogen]]ic signalling by [[apoptotic]] cells. He worked for several years in the [[United Kingdom]], doing [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] (LMB) of the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] (MRC) at the [[University of Cambridge]] with [[Peter Anthony Lawrence|Peter Lawrence]].<ref name=lawrence>{{cite journal|last1=Morata|first1=G.|last2=Lawrence|first2=P. A.|s2cid=4299506|title=Control of compartment development by the engrailed gene in Drosophila|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=255|issue=5510|year=1975|pages=614–617|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/255614a0|pmid=1134551|bibcode=1975Natur.255..614M}} {{closed access}}</ref><ref name=formemrs/>

===Awards and honours===
He has been awarded numerous honorary doctorates and prizes, including the Spanish National Prize for Research in Biology (2002), the Mexico Prize for Science and Technology (2004) and the [[Prince of Asturias Prize]] for Science and Technology (2007). He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2017|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS) in 2017]].<ref name=formemrs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/gin%C3%A9s-morata-13406/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2017|title=Professor Ginés Morata ForMemRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=2016-11-11 }}}}</ref> In 2018, he was elected a foreign associate of the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]].
